narrative:

Both of those features pushed the decision toward approving you, because smaller and faster loans are generally less risky. So the denial was not due to asking too much or stretching out the repayment.

The decisive negative factor was your checking account: it is currently below zero. Among applicants, a negative balance is uncommon, and it is a strong warning sign of current financial strain. This outweighed the positive aspects of your request. In other words, your account situation alone pushed the model strongly toward the "bad credit risk" category, and that was enough to tip the overall decision against you.

To improve your chances next time, focus on getting your checking account into positive territory and keeping it there for several months. Even a small cushion or a regular salary deposit would help. Reapplying after your account has been stable may lead to a different outcome.
